skill.displayName: 弱电智能化投标决策-安防监控项目投标评估

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its bid-analysis purpose, but it automatically registers/fingerprints the device, stores an API key locally, and creates shareable reports containing signed access links without clear opt-in.

dimensions.detail: Bid-history analysis via the vendor API is coherent with the stated purpose, but automatic device registration, MAC-hash based device identification, local credential persistence, and raw signed-link sharing go beyond ordinary analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses these behaviors in its files, but it tells the agent to proceed without extra prompting for API-key discovery/auto-registration and defaults to HTML export in full mode.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown instructions and a Python HTML renderer with no third-party dependency install or hidden startup mechanism observed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network calls to the bidding API are expected, but collecting platform/architecture/MAC hash and reading/writing files under the home directory are high-sensitivity for a bid-analysis skill without explicit runtime consent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill persists an auto-issued API key in ~/.zlbx/config.json and writes reports to ~/zlbx-bid-decision-files/; reports may include signed sk URLs intended to bypass login.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the vendor service automatically creating a device-based trial account, hashing and sending a MAC-derived identifier, storing an API key under your home directory, and writing shareable HTML reports that may contain signed access links. Prefer setting ZLBX_API_KEY yourself and avoid sharing generated reports unless you understand what the signed links grant access to.
llm.findings:
[VirusTotal] expected: Telemetry is clean, with no malicious or suspicious engine detections; this supports but does not determine the verdict.
[staticScan] expected: ClawHub static scan reported clean with no reason codes, but manual review found policy-relevant behaviors in the skill instructions.
[LP3] expected: Local file reads and report writes are disclosed and partly expected, but filesystem scope is not represented in the manifest beyond the API-key environment requirement.
[TP4] expected: I downgraded this concern: the workflow and API reference do describe concrete bid-analysis steps; report rendering is also disclosed.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Verified: auto-registration sends device-derived fields to the vendor and stores the returned API key locally. This is not necessary to the core analysis when manual API-key configuration is possible.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Verified device fingerprint concern: platform, architecture, and SHA256 MAC hash are collected for free-quota device deduplication before account creation.
[SDI-2] expected: Credential lookup through ZLBX_API_KEY and ~/.zlbx/config.json is purpose-aligned authentication behavior, but the local config read/write should be clearer and user-controlled.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Verified signed-link concern: report instructions require preserving sk免登录签名 parameters in user-visible Markdown and HTML links.
[SDI-2] expected: HTML report generation is coherent with the reporting purpose and disclosed, but default persistence of potentially sensitive procurement analysis is a review concern.
[SQP-1] expected: The activation rule is broad but remains mostly within weak-current/security/intelligent-building bid evaluation; this is a scoping note rather than the main reason for Review.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Verified: when no key is found, the skill instructs automatic registration and local credential storage rather than asking the user to opt in first.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The privacy notice describes the collected device fields, but the execution flow does not require explicit consent before collection and transmission.
[SQP-2] expected: Default HTML export is disclosed and useful, but it can persist sensitive business intelligence and signed links on disk without a separate confirmation step.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending X-API-Key to the vendor API is expected for authenticated analysis; the skill also tells the agent not to expose API keys in conversation.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Verified: the artifact treats sk-bearing URLs as shareable report links. Because the text calls sk a login-bypass signature, preserving it in reports creates avoidable access-token leakage risk.
